summary: This ROS 2 Humble beginner tutorial shows how to create and run a publisher (talker) and subscriber (listener) node in C++ that exchange string messages over a topic. The visible portion covers creating the cpp_pubsub package, downloading and examining the MinimalPublisher code, and adding rclcpp and std_msgs dependencies to package.xml. The note is cut off while beginning the CMakeLists.txt step, and most of the page is site navigation.
one_line: ROS 2 Humble tutorial on writing a simple C++ publisher and subscriber, covering package creation, the MinimalPublisher node and dependency setup.
key_facts: The tutorial goal is to create and run a publisher and subscriber node using C++; it is beginner level and takes about 20 minutes.
The nodes pass string messages to each other over a topic in a simple "talker" and "listener" system.
The example code is hosted in the ros2/examples repository under rclcpp/topics on the humble branch.
The package is created in ros2_ws/src with: ros2 pkg create --build-type ament_cmake --license Apache-2.0 cpp_pubsub.
The publisher source file is downloaded as publisher_member_function.cpp from minimal_publisher/member_function.cpp using wget on Linux/macOS or curl on Windows.
The MinimalPublisher class inherits from rclcpp::Node, names the node "minimal_publisher" and initializes count_ to 0.
The publisher uses the std_msgs::msg::String type, the topic name "topic", and a queue size of 10.
A wall timer of 500ms calls timer_callback twice a second, which sets message.data to "Hello, world! " plus a counter and publishes it.
The RCLCPP_INFO macro prints every published message to the console.
In main, rclcpp::init initializes ROS 2 and rclcpp::spin starts processing node data, including timer callbacks.
The package.xml should have its description, maintainer and license tags filled in, with license Apache License 2.0.
The dependencies <depend>rclcpp</depend> and <depend>std_msgs</depend> are added after the ament_cmake buildtool dependency in package.xml.
The tutorial page is for the Humble Hawksbill distribution, an older but still supported version; Iron is the latest linked.
